mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5%, it indicates a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces consumer and business spending, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If SPX posts positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of cases when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate (UNRATE below 4%) signals a strong labor market, which increases consumer spending and corporate revenues, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of low UNRATE (t-test p > 0.05), the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST above 1200) indicates strong demand in the housing market, which spills over into broader economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST rises above 1200 but SPX posts negative 60-day returns in more than 30% of cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Growth in industrial production (INDPRO increasing by more than 0.5% month-over-month) signals increased economic activity and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO growth is accompanied by negative SPX returns in more than 40% of cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When both GDP (GDPC1) and retail sales (RSAFS) show concurrent growth, it indicates strong aggregate demand, which drives corporate revenues and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 and RSAFS both grow but SPX posts negative 20-day returns in more than 30% of cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A slowdown in GDP growth (GDPC1 growth below 2% annualized) signals weakening demand, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 growth is below 2% but SPX posts positive 60-day returns in more than 40% of cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary easing cycle, a combination of low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS below 1%) and rising consumer prices (CPIAUCSL increasing by more than 0.2% month-over-month) signals inflationary pressures that erode real returns, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If both FEDFUNDS is below 1% and CPIAUCSL is rising but SPX posts positive 20-day returns in more than 30% of cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When both unemployment (UNRATE below 4.5%) and payroll employment (PAYEMS increasing by more than 100,000 jobs) are strong, it signals a tight labor market that supports consumer spending and corporate revenues, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If both UNRATE is below 4.5% and PAYEMS is growing but SPX posts negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of cases, the hypothesis is rejected.
